Suggestions are welcome.

description_text: This structure is modeled after a 1/2" scale doll house that I recently built.  POS kit!   It is 18X12X24. It looks like the doll house except that the dormer and the chimney on the left are reversed with the chimney continued downward.  The bay is a completion of 2 bays on the rite on the doll house.  And it also has a back wall, which the doll house does not have.  Centre hall floor plan, 5 bedrooms, 3.5 baths, living room, dining and kitchen plus an optional cellar.  The doll house has much more gingerbread, which you can add if you want to.  Also you can add cabinets and plumbing fixtures plus more interior detailing.  I love to build models of all types, This doll house goes to my brother's daughter's daughter someday. I left it raw plywood.  She is 2, so not old enough yet, I think.  Have fun, there is also a shell of this structure.

description_text: This may be my last model for a while.  Reason: my cancer is back and is all over the place.  Not sure what I am going to do about that.  With that in mind, this is another split level.  I love this style of house. (Obviously)  This is a 4 level house with a detailed elevator.  Turn off the lift via layer to see the reclaimed service station hydralic lift.  This also has a seperate dining room with soffit liting and an office with a large storage closet.  Mud room off the garage with pantry and bath.  Theatre has 7.1 surround sound.  The side center speakers are in the ceiling.  There is large multi-purpose room with a 10' ceiling.(lowest level)  The house has about 4,000 square feet on 4 levels.  Rest of the house is fairly standard.  This could be built without the lowest level as well as a larger garage.  Have fun, I have enjoyed presenting these models for you to look at.  Bob---  update:  thanks for the ecouragement.  I will make more models if I can.

description_text: Another kit house from the 1930s.  This may be a Sears house.  It was on the Sears site.  The plan for the Livingroom called for beams and panneling, so that is what I did.  Also added a custom ceiling in the Dining room.  Did not find the laundry room, so I put hook  ups for the washer and dryer in the garage.  Carved out space above the garage for Master Bedroom bath and closet.  I few minor changes here and there, updated interior slightly.  Attic access in upstairs hall.

description_text: China Airlines Dreamliner 744. China Airlines is the national airlines of Taiwan. In 2004 the airlines received a unique 747-400 featuring a livery that combined the airline's plum blossom tail image with Boeing's new blue commercial airplane livery. The airplane was part of the last 744 passenger version order, and was the first CAL special livery jet that ever took flight (First special livery was the "Taiwan Touch Your Heart" jet but the livery was removed before the plane even rolled out from the paint shop). Many regarded the plane as the most beautiful 747, however, in 2012, the plane was repainted into the normal CAL scheme, and the iconic dynasty dreamliner went into history. Thanks to WilliamT for the superb 744 :D

A mosque is a place of worship for Muslims. There are strict and detailed requirements in Sunni jurisprudence  for a place of worship to be considered a mosque, with places that do not meet these requirements regarded as musallas. description_text:
This Lamp began as a test Vase to be honest. I wanted to test a new printer and this “Vase” was one of the Test models I made. I liked it so much that I turned it into a Lamp. 
To do this I made a simple “ base “. There are 2. The one I used is “base 6mm.stl”, but If you want to scale down, “base 21mm.stl” might be better (In the “base” is a small cavity where the connector of the LED strip is housed. If you scale down the base to much, this cavity might become to small for the connector).The (in Translucent Blue PET-G) Printed Vase sits on this Base. Then in the Vase an Aluminum tube is bolted down using an M4x40 bolt, nut and printed parts “tube plug lamp.stl”. An LED strip (15meters) is wrapped around this tube, making the light source. To get a better the idea how this all comes together, please see the Photos in the Photo section.
The Aluminum tube I used is 490mm high and has an outer diameter of  34mm.The Lamp Shade (or Vase) is 558.7mm high. Yes I had to scale it down because there was not enough Filament on any Roll at the time :-) At 100% scale it is 705.871mm high.Note that the Lamp Shade (or Vase) is printed using the “Spiral Outer Contour” mode in Cura.The Nozzle I used is 0.8mm. With smaller Nozzle sizes the print will warp at this size.
So for most people its not going to work. I Also printed this model at 240mm high and it worked out super nice. For this small one I used a 0.4mm Nozzle.
Then I Also experimented with a “diffuser”. This is simply a cylinder that fits around the aluminum (with the LED strip) Tube. The Idea is to spread the light form the LEDs a bit better. Hoping the individual LEDs can not be spot trough the Lamp Shade (or Vase) anymore. I printed it in Translucent PET-G and it did not work very good. The LEDs still can be identified as individual light spots in the Lamp Shade. Maybe just white PLA will do a better job. But I just experimented with spray painting mine white. It works out, but more paint means less Light. The distance of the diffuser to the LEDs also is very important. If this distance is to short the diffuser also doesn't work.
Anyhow, You can make it as difficult as You want I guess. The simples way is to just print “giant vase2.stl” en the “base”. Put them together with a lamp of choice inside :-)
Feel free to ask any questions or constructive comments :-)

The per capita income for the town was $35,714. About 5.9% of families and 11.1% of the population were below the poverty line, including 16.7% of those under the age of 18 and 8.3% of those 65 or over.

description_text:
The Pipo Chair is conceived as a wooden surface that integrates armchairs and seat from the same material. The idea is to create a monolithic piece from one material that opens in the outside and stretches in the center. The way you can see through the armchairs gesture evokes a simple movement that lets light pass through it. Using technology to produce the chair with a conscious use of materials was our main goal for this piece. The chair is made out of two sheets of plywood. Composed of 29 main curved sections that are cut into two or three pieces overlapped, making it very efficient in the use of material. Water base coat.
Model originally created in Blender3D and rendered with Cycles.

description_text: The Parthenon is a former temple on the Athenian Acropolis, Greece, dedicated to the goddess Athena, whom the people of Athens considered their patron. Construction began in 447 BC when the Athenian Empire was at the peak of its power. It was completed in 438 BC, although decoration of the building continued until 432 BC. It is the most important surviving building of Classical Greece, generally considered the zenith of the Doric order. Its decorative sculptures are considered some of the high points of Greek art. The Parthenon is regarded as an enduring symbol of Ancient Greece, Athenian democracy and Western civilization, and one of the world's greatest cultural monuments. To the Athenians who built it, the Parthenon and other Periclean monuments of the Acropolis were seen fundamentally as a celebration of Hellenic victory over the Persian invaders and as a thanksgiving to the gods for that victory.

This is a Cubic Glass/Pot 3D model, useful for example for any home scene or other, you can use it as a bowl, as a vase or as a structure to add it to another model as well of course.
This is a model wich has no textures or material applied to it, you would customize it yourself. The advantage is that, in case you want to apply your own textures and materials, buying this one is cheaper than buying a version of it wich has textures or materials applied to it.
This model is the most low poly it can be so it is useful if you want a vase/glass/pot shape to custom the way you want to, in order to get the amount of vertices and polygons you want to have after Subdisvion Surface modifer for exemple.
Only a Solidify modifier has been applied to the object to get the bowl/vase density aspect.
The model is about 10 cm of lenght and 11,5 of diameter so it is 10 x 11,5 x 11,5 cm ready to be 3D printed, all 3d files are avaibleand can be used for digital purpose as well of course.
It is 576 vertices and 546 polygons.
I am at your disposal if you have any question.
Enjoy ! Thanks.

description_text:
This free sample contains just 2 out of the 19 sockets and switches available in the main product - the Single Rocker Switch and the Singe Euro Socket. They do however have the same, full range of materials of the final product outlined in the description below, which is an edited version of the description of the main product.
D&R Sockets and Toggle, Rocker and Dimmer Switches FREE SAMPLE
Introduction
This collection of sockets and switches is designed to help bring those all important finishing touches to your renders. Be it an architectural visualisation of a luxury apartment,an interior for an art project or any other scene, these details can make all the difference.They come in 3 brushed metal and 2 non metal finishes, which can be mixed and matched to create the look you desire.
Switches
The light switches come in Toggle, Rocker and Dimmer varieties. All the switches are available in single, double, triple and quadruple switches per faceplate.The faceplates and switches are coloured separately. There are 5 colours available  – Black, White and brushed metal in Gold, Silver and Copper. You can mix and match any combination of these colours. So there are 25 combinations to choose from. (Some, but not all of these can be seen in the pictures provided on the website.)
Sockets
The sockets have faceplates available in the same 5 materials.As the trim of the sockets themselves should not be metal, it is available in black and white only, giving 10 material combinations to choose from.The Sockets come in single and double versions. The UK sockets are available with and without switches.
Directions
Importing the switches or sockets into your 3D programme of choice
Open your 3D package and click on the Import option.
Browse your hard drive to where you saved the .obj and/or .fbx files, select which of these 2 you want and click import.The objects will appear in the arrangement seen in the product photos provided on the web site, not all overlapping at the origin, to make it easier to see and select them.The origin of each object is situated in the centre of the faceplate when viewed from the front and in line with the back of the faceplate i.e. level with the wall surface the object is going to be fixed to.To build the material, add a shader and plug in the desired Colour, Metallic, Normal, Roughness and Specular Maps into the corresponding input on the shader node. You will find more information on these maps later in this document.If you need further help importing the objects or creating a material, look at the documentation for your specific software for more details.
Materials
Switches
As mentioned above and as can be seen in the product pictures, the faceplate and the switches themselves can have different materials. There are 5 materials available - Black, White, Gold, Silver and Copper. You can mix and match these in any combination. So, for each faceplate material, you can choose any material for the Switches. Giving a total of 25 combinations to choose from.You will find Colour, Roughness, Specular, Metallic and Normal Maps included for all possible combinations of materials for each item.
For the Colour : -
Each material has its own colour, meaning there are 25 colour combinations and a corresponding Colour Map for each. These are all 1k, as a higher resolution is not needed.
For Roughness, Specular and Metallic, there is a choice of 4 UV maps: -
Non Metallic faceplate and a NonMetallic switchNon Metallic faceplate and a Metallic switchMetallic faceplate and a Non Metallic switchMetallic faceplate and a Metallic switch
These are also all 1k maps. Be sure to choose the correct one to match the material combination you are using.The Normal Maps are available in 1k, 2k and 4k.All the renders in the example pictures were done using the 4k maps because they are close up pictures and the larger normal map provides more detail. 
To summarise, there are 25 Colour maps, 4 Roughness maps, 4 Specular maps , 4 Metallic maps and 12 Normal maps for each Switch.
Sockets
As mentioned above, the choice for the trim of the Sockets is limited to non metallic materials.The sockets have 10 material combinations available with 10 colour maps, 2 Roughness maps, 2 Specular maps , 2 Metallic maps and 6 Normal maps.

Ring LampThis is a lamp inspired by a Vase. It is build up out of 27 rings that are equally spaced from each other. This creates a ring shadow effect on the surrounding walls that is very nice.This Lamp can be used in 2 ways: You can put it aside you bed or hang it on the ceiling. The dimensions of the Lamp are about 180x180mm and 294mm high.
Assembling this lampAs a light source it uses a standard light bulb. That makes it easy for everyone to make this Lamp. You can choose any lamp bulb you like, as long as it fits. I used a E14 fitting, but a E27 should also fit. Of course beware with glowing bulbs and their heat... the plastic may melt. In my case it is a thing because the lamp is 3d printed out of PLA. But if you are going to used LED, you are save :-). It took me 51,5 hours to print this lamp. I used 481 gram of filament. For more details you can take a look at the photo section. I have included some data from printing to give you an idea where these hours and grams come from ;-)
Amount of Filament & parts needed:2x M3x16mm bolt2x M3 nut1x power cord (optional with a switch)1x lamp fitting (I used a E14, but you can use anything that fits)1x A bulb that fits your fitting+/-500 gram filament.
The Assembly of this lampTo give you an idea how to assemble the ring lamp, please take a look at images in the photo section. I made 10 steps you can follow. Step 1: Print the 37 parts of the lamp that are shown here.Step 2: Glue the parts “arm1.stl” & “arm2.stl” together. You have to do this 3 times. I used Super Glue for this.Step 3: Push all the rings (except ring1) into the slots of the “arms” as shown in this image. Start with only 2 arms to make it a bit easier. Make sure all the rings are in the right order.Step 4: After the 26 rings are pushed into the slots of the 2 arms it should look like this. Now the last arm can go in.Step 5: It looks like this from the bottom, when the last arm is installed. Now ring1 can go on to fix the arms in place as shown in “#Step 6”.Step6: Here you see the lamp from the top. Now ring1 can be place on the end of the 3 arms.Step7: When ring1.stl is mounted, the white part (lock ring1.stl) should fit inside. “Lock ring1.stl” is hold in place by “lock ring2.stl”. When lock ring2.stl is turned, it locks the arms in place. Here you see lock ring2 in the locked position.Step8: Now the part “cable lock.stl” can be installed. It acts as a strain relief for the cable. To install it, you need 2 M3x16mm bolts and 2 M3 nuts.Step9: Time to install a cable that goes to the lamp. Mine already has a switch in the cable. Tighten the bolts to hold the cable in place.Step10: Install the lamp socket and the lamp. After that the Ring Lamp is done :-). I used a E14 fitting and an old style light bulb. 
To get a better idea, please look at the added images in the photo section
Of course feel free to ask any question, in case my summary is not clear :-)
